mcqs.question: Which description correctly visualises a configuration where three lines intersect at three different points (no two lines are parallel and no three meet at a single point)?

options.A: All three lines meet at one common point.
options.B: The three lines form the sides of a triangle.
options.C: Each pair of lines meets at a distinct point, giving three intersection points.
options.D: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts across them.

mcqs.answer: Each pair of lines meets at a distinct point, giving three intersection points.
mcqs.explanation: When three lines are neither parallel nor concurrent, each pair intersects once, producing three separate intersection points. Option C describes this correctly. Option A describes concurrency, B describes a closed triangle (which is not about line intersections), and D mentions parallelism, which is not part of the required configuration.

mcqs.question: Line l1 meets line l2 at point P, line l2 meets line l3 at point Q, and line l1 meets line l3 at point R. How many distinct intersection points are there among the three lines?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of lines intersects once, giving three different points: P, Q, and R. Hence there are three distinct intersection points. The other numbers would imply missing or extra intersections, which is not the case here.

mcqs.question: If three different lines intersect at a single point O, how many angles are formed at O?
mcqs.explanation: When three lines cross at one point, they divide the plane into six equal angular regions, i.e., six angles. Four angles would be the case for two intersecting lines, and eight would require four lines.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line A is drawn horizontally, line B slopes upward and crosses line A, and line C is drawn vertically crossing both A and B. Which statement best describes the arrangement of the three lines?

options.A: All three lines are parallel to each other.
options.B: Two lines intersect at one point while the third line is parallel to both.
options.C: Each pair of lines intersects at a different point.
options.D: All three lines intersect at the same single point.

mcqs.answer: Each pair of lines intersects at a different point.
mcqs.explanation: Line A meets B at one point, A meets C at another, and B meets C at a third point. Hence every pair has its own intersection, matching option C. The other options describe parallelism or concurrency, which are not present.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that three distinct lines can intersect at exactly two different points. Which statement correctly clarifies this misconception?

options.A: It can happen if two of the lines coincide.
options.B: It occurs when one line passes through the intersection of the other two.
options.C: Three distinct lines intersect at three points unless they are concurrent at a single point.
options.D: Three lines can intersect at only one point.

mcqs.answer: Three distinct lines intersect at three points unless they are concurrent at a single point.
mcqs.explanation: For three distinct, non‑parallel lines, each pair meets once, giving three intersection points. Only when all three are concurrent do they share a single point. Option C states this correctly. Options A and B involve special cases (coincident lines or one line through another intersection) that change the count of distinct lines, and D ignores the usual pairwise intersections.

mcqs.question: Line AB is drawn horizontally. Line CD is drawn vertically and crosses AB at point X. Line EF is drawn slanting so that it crosses AB at point Y and also crosses CD at point Z. How many distinct intersection points are formed by the three lines?
mcqs.explanation: The three intersection points are X (AB ∩ CD), Y (AB ∩ EF), and Z (CD ∩ EF). No other crossings occur, so there are exactly three distinct points. Options A, C, and D either miss a point or add non‑existent ones.

mcqs.question:
Compare the total number of angles formed in the two configurations below:
1) Three lines intersect at a single common point.
2) Three lines intersect pairwise at three different points (no two are parallel, no three are concurrent).
Which configuration yields a greater total number of angles?

options.A: Both configurations produce the same total number of angles.
options.B: The single‑point configuration produces more angles.
options.C: The pairwise‑intersection configuration produces more angles.
options.D: There is not enough information to decide.

mcqs.answer: The pairwise‑intersection configuration produces more angles.
mcqs.explanation: When three lines meet at one point, they create six angles. In the pairwise case, each of the three intersection points gives four angles, totaling twelve angles. Therefore, the configuration with three separate intersections yields more angles, making option C correct. Options A and B underestimate the count, and D is unnecessary because the information given is sufficient.

mcqs.question: In a competitive‑exam diagram, line p is drawn parallel to line q, and line r cuts across both p and q. Which description best matches this arrangement?

options.A: All three lines intersect at a single point.
options.B: Two lines are parallel and the third line acts as a transversal.
options.C: No two lines are parallel; each pair meets at a different point.
options.D: All three lines are parallel to each other.

mcqs.answer: Two lines are parallel and the third line acts as a transversal.
mcqs.explanation: Lines p and q are given as parallel. Line r intersecting both of them is the definition of a transversal. Hence option B accurately describes the arrangement. Options A and D contradict the parallel condition, and C ignores the stated parallelism.
